_comment: Round 4 of the de-ossification port: 27 functions across three classes, chosen for being
small, leaf-like and completely explainable rather than for being large.
code/midtown2/mmai/aiintersection.cpp   18 of aiIntersection's 29 functions
code/midtown2/mod/modstatic.cpp          2 of modStatic's 10
code/midtown2/mmgame/mmjaxis.cpp         all 7 of mmJaxis - the whole class
tools/build.py folds every data/ported_*.json into data/ported.json at step 1, before it runs
genheaders.py and before tools/asm.py, so this file only has to sit in data/ - do not merge it
by hand. The three headers have already been flipped to ARTS_EXPORT and asm.py stops the build
on an export that ported.json does not list, so the two must travel together.

data/ported.json already carries these 27, because tools/verify_extents.py reads that file and nothing else, so the verifier run merged them - exactly the state every other data/ported_*.json is already in (all 133 of their symbols are duplicated there too). build.py's merge is a no-op for them and reports them on its `duplicate symbols across ported lists` line, as it already does for the earlier rounds.
METHOD. Every body was disassembled with capstone 5.0.7 over the bytes of midtown2.exe at the
RVA midtown2.map gives. Nothing was transcribed from MM2_RE_KIT - Trap 4 (11,900 foreign
identifiers reaching inside correctly-named functions) makes the aiIntersection pseudocode
unusable for member offsets, and no pseudocode was consulted for any of the 27.
VERIFIERS. With this file merged into data/ported.json:
verify_extents.py  214 ported functions checked, PASS - no dword in .rdata or .data points
strictly inside any of them. Cross-checked independently against the RE
kit's _INDEX.csv: no kit function starts inside any of the 27 extents,
which is the Trap 7 check (Vector3::Dot3x3Transpose's four absorbed
static constructors are the reason it exists).
verify_arity.py    6315 agree, 12 MISMATCH, 417 skipped - byte for byte the pre-existing
Trap 14 list. None of the 27 appears in the mismatch list OR in the
skipped list, so all 27 were actively checked and agree.
ARITY IS NOT SUFFICIENT (Trap 14's own warning), so every argument was checked for how it is
USED and every body for whether it does what its verb says:
Road/Path(i32)                   the argument indexes, it is never dereferenced
NumAvailSinks(aiPath*)           compared as a pointer against each element
Add/RemoveVehicle/Banger(...)    stored into and unlinked from a list, as pointers
AddRoad(aiPath*)                 stored into the grown array
StopSources(i32)                 forwarded unchanged to aiPath::AllwaysStop(i32)
aiIntersection(i32)              `mov cx, word ptr [ebp+8]` - an int truncated to its low word
SetRange(f32,f32)/Normalize(f32) `fld dword ptr [ebp+8]` - loaded as floats, not addresses
NormalizePOV(u32)                `mov eax,[ebp+8]` then `cmp ax,0xFFFF` and `fild qword` - an
integer used as a value
ODDITIES REPRODUCED RATHER THAN FIXED. Each of these is a place where idiomatic C++ would have
differed from the 1999 code, which is the failure mode that quarantined the Matrix33 round:
aiIntersection::Road and ::Path bound the index with `jg`, not `jge`, so index == RoadCount
passes the guard and reads one past the end. Kept.
aiIntersection::aiIntersection writes only 0x12, 0x04, 0x20 and 0x10. Roads, PrevVeh,
NextVeh, Center, Vehicles and Bangers are born holding whatever the allocator last left
there - memMemoryAllocator::Allocate does not zero (Trap 12). Kept.
aiIntersection::SetFourWay clears the BANGER list before forwarding to the traffic lights,
which reads as unrelated and is exactly what `mov dword ptr [ecx+0x28], 0` does. Kept.
aiIntersection::NumOneWays dereferences every element with no null test, unlike Road. Kept.
modStatic::GetTriCount is `(n * 21846) >> 16`, NOT `n / 3`. The two agree only while n is at
most 32767 and the magic is one low from 32768 up. Written as the multiply.
mmJaxis::Capture uses `fcom` + `test ah, 1` - C0 alone, which is set by a LESS-THAN compare
and by an UNORDERED one, so the original returns -1 for a NaN reading. Written
`if (!(moved >= CaptureLo))` and not `if (moved < CaptureLo)`, because the plain form is
false for a NaN and would return 0. This is the same instruction pattern, and the same trap,
as the Matrix33::IsZero change named in wip/README.md as the prime suspect for that crash.
mmJaxis::NormalizePOV compares only the LOW SIXTEEN BITS against 0xFFFF, so 0x0000FFFF is
treated as centred just like DirectInput's 0xFFFFFFFF. Kept as a 16-bit comparison.
mmJaxis::mmJaxis leaves CaptureLo and CaptureHi uninitialised. Kept.
WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT AS ARTS_IMPORT, and why - the reasoning is in the source too:
?Reset@aiIntersection@@QAEXXZ  tail-jumps `[[eax]+0xC]`, slot 3 of aiTrafficLightSet.
??1aiIntersection@@QAE@XZ      calls asNode::RemoveChild then slot 0, the deleting dtor.
?StopSignOkayToGo@...          calls slots 11 and 18 of aiVehicle.
A virtual call written in C++ takes its slot index from the DECLARATION ORDER of the base's
virtuals, and `py tools/asm_vtables.py --check asNode` says asnode.h declares its eleven
virtuals ALPHABETICALLY - not in the order the binary's table has them - and additionally
declares a twelfth (?GetClassNameA@) that occupies no slot at all. Every one of those calls
would land on the wrong entry with nothing to notice. aiTrafficLightSet itself checks OK, so
the non-virtual ?SetFourWay@aiTrafficLightSet@@QAEXXZ IS called, as a direct call.
Init, ReadBinary and AddBangersToObsMap each own an _SEH funclet symbol of their own
(Trap 10) and are left alone with it. CreateRoadMap, SaveBinary, Dump's larger neighbours
and the three IsXxxStart predicates are simply outside this round's remit.
LAYOUT WORK. data/layouts_round4.json retypes mmJaxis, and data/layouts.json has been updated
from it. tools/ctor_layouts.py had all seven offsets and the 0x1C size right but typed the
first four as i32 - a constructor storing a dword of zero cannot say whether the dword is an
integer or a float - and left 0x10/0x14 as one opaque `u8 field_10[8]` because no constructor
writes them. Every function in the class reads those offsets with x87 instructions, and
ResetCapture writes 0x10 and 0x14 as two separate dwords. OFFSETS AND SIZE ARE UNCHANGED, so
nothing in the binary moves; only the C++ spelling of the fields changed. The three headers as
committed are byte-identical to what tools/genheaders.py regenerates from the updated
layouts.json plus this file - that was checked by driving genheaders' own emit_class() and
diffing, not by eye.
gfx/gfxpacket.h IS NOT INCLUDED by modstatic.cpp, on purpose. It does not compile - line 38
declares a parameter as `unsigned const i16*`, and `unsigned` cannot be applied to a
typedef-name - and four of its member NAMES are wrong (docs/gfx_layouts.md 16.1). The two
fields the counters need are mirrored in modstatic.cpp at their proven offsets with
static_asserts, the same way agigl/glpacket.h does it and for the same reasons.
NOT COMPILED AND NOT RUN. Per this round's brief, nothing here has been through cl.exe or the
game. aiIntersection and modStatic are city-AI and model-drawing code that the current
menu-only boot does not reach, so a working-game bisect will not exercise them; mmJaxis is
reachable through mmInput as soon as a joystick axis is polled.
